steps.what: Direct activities of laboratory workers and resolve questions about execution

tasks.design: Keep direction and clarification with the supervising technician. Existing laboratory work information in {DOCS} supports discussion; the task establishes no separate roster or copying baseline to remove.
tasks.previous_blocker: Worker readiness and method questions require contextual supervision.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability removes the stated supervision work.
tasks.still_hard: Competence, equipment availability and unexpected results change what work is appropriate.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a worker needs clarification or work must pause.
tasks.altitude: Supervision responsibilities and time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: How method deviations affect work allocation

evidence.claim: Laboratory direction requires contextual supervision; a separate reducible scheduling baseline is not established by this task.

assumptions: Boundary is technician direction, excluding workers' laboratory execution and personnel evaluation. Their effort remains unchanged outside this focal denominator.

The laboratory lead supplies current work requirements before s1. Workers supply progress and questions during s1 before the technician confirms directions. Readiness and competence checks remain within its full time; no structured qualified-worker flag is assumed.
Native work visibility precedes custom code. No new tool or transferred work is proposed, so upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Does observed supervision contain repeated clerical allocation work separate from necessary direction?

approvals.approved_version: Exact worker, activity, method version, conditions and direction communicated by the technician; changed conditions require a new direction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0 and net=0. Human supervision retains all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess environmental impacts of process changes

steps.what: Analyze potential environmental impacts of proposed production process changes
Recommend steps to mitigate negative environmental impacts

tasks.design: Retain impact analysis and mitigation recommendations with the technician under scientific direction. Proposal and evidence access in {DOCS} support the work, but a separate drafting or fixed-calculation baseline is not established.
tasks.previous_blocker: A changed process can create site-specific environmental pathways not captured in a generic checklist.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability establishes a reduction in the stated judgement actions.
tasks.still_hard: Mitigation effectiveness depends on process behavior, receptors and evidence gaps.
tasks.human_edge: Identify overlooked pathways and distinguish an option from a defensible recommendation.
tasks.altitude: Analysis and recommendation rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: How uncertainty and receptor sensitivity affect mitigation choice

evidence.claim: Site-specific impact analysis and mitigation choice remain judgement work without an established repeated assembly substep.

assumptions: Boundary is assessment and recommendation, excluding implementation and management authorization. Subsequent scientific and operational decisions remain unchanged outside this task.

The process engineer provides the proposed configuration, materials, throughput and operating conditions before s1; the technician verifies scope and evidence during s1. Operations supplies constraints during s2 before recommendations close. No free impact severity or feasible-mitigation flag is assumed.
Consider native evidence retrieval before code if a distinct repetitive burden is measured. No new tool or ongoing upkeep is proposed; incremental hours are zero.
unknowns: Available process change data and delegated assessment scope
research_questions: Which past mitigation decisions depended on site evidence absent from the original proposal?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0 and net=0. No invented report-writing share is removed from impact assessment.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assess evidence, delegated authority and procedure for establishments violating environmental or health regulations
Initiate the authorized procedure or refer the evidence to the competent authority

tasks.design: Keep evidence assessment and authorized initiation with the responsible person. {DOCS} supplies case material; no automatic penalty, closure decision or external filing is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Jurisdiction, evidence and procedural rights determine whether initiation is appropriate.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability establishes a reducible clerical share within this occasional action.
tasks.still_hard: The technician may lack enforcement authority and need to refer rather than initiate sanctions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize authority limits and ensure the action matches the evidence and procedure.
tasks.altitude: Authority remains limited to the existing delegated role.

reach.learn: How to distinguish evidence referral from a sanction decision

evidence.claim: Procedure initiation requires checking actual delegated authority; a technician in an ordinary private company is not assumed to have power to fine or close another establishment.

assumptions: Boundary ends at authorized initiation or evidence referral, excluding the authority's final sanction, legal review and closure execution. National rules and actual delegation must be confirmed locally.

Investigators produce evidence before s1; the competent body supplies current procedure and delegation before action. The technician checks establishment identity, evidence provenance, scope and authority within s1; s2 includes recipient confirmation and communication capture. No free violation-proven or sanction-authorized flag is assumed.
Native case access precedes code. No new service or work transfer is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Does this role initiate a formal procedure or only send evidence to an authorized body?

already_counted.description: Authorized initiation or referral and receipt clarification

approvals.approved_version: Exact establishment, evidence version, delegated scope, recipient and procedure initiation or referral communicated; changes require renewed approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0 and net=0. Authority checks and procedural communication retain time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Determine suitable kinds of chemicals and verify the purification treatment basis
Calculate amounts from the selected treatment method and verified quantities
Assess and accept the proposed chemical amount and treatment conditions

tasks.design: Configure prescribed treatment arithmetic in {SPREADSHEET} after the technician selects and verifies the treatment basis. Keep chemical choice, suitability assessment and recommendation with the technician; operational dosing remains outside this draft-only design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected method parameters still needed repeated arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: A fixed formula can calculate a quantity without selecting the chemical or asserting safety.
tasks.still_hard: Organism, impurity, system compatibility and changing conditions affect treatment suitability.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a calculated quantity is unsuitable despite correct arithmetic.
tasks.altitude: Potentially less manual arithmetic; treatment judgement and authorization remain unchanged.

reach.learn: How concentration, contact time and system conditions limit treatment choices

evidence.claim: Prescribed treatment arithmetic can be configured from verified parameters; this does not establish automated chemical selection or safe dosing capability.

assumptions: Boundary is determination and recommendation, excluding chemical procurement, application, control-system operation and final scientific authorization. Those actors retain their existing work.

The responsible scientist supplies the method and limits before s1. In s1 the technician captures system volume or flow, selected chemical, concentration, purity, target condition, method version, formula and units after assessing current evidence; its 70 hours include measurement/source verification and capture. Missing or unsuitable parameters require manual scientific review, never an inferred safe-dose flag.
Test native approved treatment calculations before a workbook or code. Apply only to remaining manual arithmetic; no existing instrument or control-system runtime is claimed as labour saved.
research_questions: Does manual treatment arithmetic remain after current approved tools are considered?

already_counted.description: Chemical selection, condition assessment and field capture

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=90, gross=10, upkeep=4, net=6. Range 0-2 allows existing calculation coverage or little arithmetic relative to treatment judgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Supervision, environmental assessment and enforcement boundaries stay human; any residual prescribed treatment arithmetic may shrink.
reach: Work with an environmental scientist on mitigation evidence
Learn treatment compatibility with a chemical technician
role.ambitious_version: A technician who makes traceable recommendations while retaining careful scientific and procedural judgement.
